title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Tabcorp Directors. Subject to Blackout Periods, prior written approval to deal (Chairman, or Chairman of the Audit Committee if the Chairman is dealing), short-term dealing and short-selling prohibitions, margin lending/security interest prohibitions, Minimum Shareholding Policy compliance, and post-trade notification within two business days.

tiers.name: Restricted Employees
tiers.description: Executives reporting directly to the MD & CEO (ELT members), team members reporting directly to ELT members, and any other team member determined by the Board, Chairman or MD & CEO to be a Restricted Employee. Subject to the same Blackout Period, approval, short-term dealing, short-selling, and margin lending/security interest prohibitions as Directors.

tiers.name: team members
tiers.description: All Directors, employees and contractors of Tabcorp. Subject only to the general prohibition on dealing while in possession of inside information; no prior-approval regime, Blackout Period, short-term dealing or margin lending prohibition applies to this tier unless the person is also a Director or Restricted Employee.

tiers.name: Plan participants
tiers.description: Team members participating in any of Tabcorp's employee or executive equity or incentive plans. Restricted from hedging or entering a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under those plans.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Any person or entity which might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with Tabcorp or any of its Directors or team members, such as spouses, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, or joint venture partners.

windows.end_anchor: End of the day Tabcorp releases its half yearly results (inclusive)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Tabcorp Board or Chairman may impose 'Other Periods' at their absolute discretion and without prior notice; the policy does not state whether such a period is disclosed or kept confidential.

rules.section: Prohibition on hedging and derivatives
rules.detail: Absolute ban on derivative arrangements over restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under Tabcorp's equity or incentive plans.
rules.evidence: must not enter into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.

rules.section: Key definitions; Directors and Restricted Employees need approval to deal
rules.detail: No express derivatives rule for Directors outside the plan-securities ban. Creating a hedge or other financial interest over securities is a dealing; Securities expressly includes derivatives (equity swaps, CFDs, futures, ETO/OTC options), so an OTC put/call requires prior written approval from the Chairman, is barred in Blackout Periods, and lapses if inside information is later held.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to securities

rules.section: Key definitions; Directors and Restricted Employees need approval to deal

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Referenced by cross-reference to the Non Executive Director Shareholding Policy and Executive Shareholding Policy; approval to deal may be refused if the applicant is not, or would not remain, compliant with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy. Silent on whether hedged or collared shares are excluded from the calculation.

exemption_authority: The applicable approver (Chairman for Directors; Company Secretary or MD & CEO for Restricted Employees) may permit dealing in a Blackout Period or on a short-term basis only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a court order) and only where the trade is the only reasonable course of action available; refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the applicant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Tabcorp securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Tabcorp securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The unqualified ban on granting a lender any rights over Tabcorp securities is not limited to acquisition financing, so it appears to catch a bank's security interest over already-vested, collared shares and blocks the loan leg outright for Directors and Restricted Employees.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any trading that is the subject of approval must be executed within five business days of the receipt of the written approval (unless the approval is withdrawn).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both derivative legs of a cleared collar must be priced and executed within five business days of approval, a tight window for negotiating bank documentation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval is withdrawn or refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank structuring the collar may never be told why clearance was refused, complicating any attempt to restructure around a refusal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An application for approval to deal in Tabcorp securities may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed dealing will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If exercise of the written call could cause a disposal that breaches the director's or executive's Minimum Shareholding Policy, approval for the collar could be refused up front.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no exception permitting a lender's forced sale of securities during a Blackout Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Absent an express carve-out, enforcement or physical settlement by the bank during a Blackout Period is not clearly excused, so unwind mechanics would need to be timed to open windows.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Directors or Restricted Employees under this policy, even though the derivative legs alone would be approvable. The put and call are 'dealings' under the broad definition (creating a hedge or other financial interest) and so require prior written approval from the Chairman (Directors) or the Company Secretary/MD & CEO (Restricted Employees), execution within five business days of approval, and avoidance of the half-year, full-year, AGM and any ad hoc Blackout Periods and of inside information. The loan leg fails outright: the policy separately and unconditionally prohibits Directors and Restricted Employees (and their associates) from granting a lender any rights over their Tabcorp securities, a ban that is not limited to acquisition financing and has no exemption authority or clearance route. Only unvested performance rights/options and restricted plan shares are absolutely barred from any hedge or derivative; vested, unrestricted shares are otherwise only subject to the general dealing/approval regime. General 'team members' outside these two tiers face no approval regime and no secured-financing ban, but they also have no unvested equity incentives typically at stake and are an unlikely collar counterparty. Refusals of approval are confidential and approval can also be refused for non-compliance with the separate Minimum Shareholding Policies.
